record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.context_brief: Overt choice on non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces
record.original_question: For overt choice VC_X on non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces X, can this principle be classified more precisely than the currently known bounds LPO ≤W VC_X ≤W (isEmpty : \A(N^N) → S)?

evidence.quote: For overt choice VCX for non-Fr´echet-Urysohn coPolish spaces X we only know that LPO ≤W VCX ≤W (isEmpty :\A(NN) → S) – which is perfectly compatible with VCX being a familiar Weihrauch degree, and is a remarkably weak classification.
Open Question 4 (de Brecht, Schr¨oder & P. [9]). Can we classify overt choice for non-Fr´echet-Urysohn coPolish spaces more precisely?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A represented space is a pair (X, δ_X) where δ_X is a partial surjection from Baire space N^N onto X. A multivalued function f : ⊆ X ⇒ Y between represented spaces is Weihrauch reducible to g : ⊆ Z ⇒ W, written f ≤_W g, if there are computable functions H, K : ⊆ N^N → N^N such that whenever G is a realizer of g (i.e. G(z) is a name of some w ∈ g(δ_Z(z))), the map p ↦ H(p, G(K(p))) is a realizer of f.

A topological space X is Fréchet–Urysohn if for every A ⊆ X and every x in the closure of A, there is a sequence in A converging to x. A space is coPolish if it is the colimit of an increasing sequence of Polish subspaces with appropriate compatibility (equivalently, a quasi-Polish countably tight cb_0 space arising as a sequential colimit of Polish spaces); examples include the space of polynomials with the colimit topology of finite-dimensional subspaces.

For a represented space X, let A(X) denote the hyperspace of closed subsets represented by enumerations of basic open sets that intersect the set (the "overt" representation). The overt choice principle on X is the multivalued function
  VC_X : ⊆ A(X) ⇒ X,
sending a nonempty closed set A ∈ A(X) to any element of A.

The Weihrauch degree LPO is represented by the limited principle of omniscience
  LPO : N^N → {0,1}, p ↦ 1 if p = 0^ω, else 0.

The principle isEmpty : A(N^N) → S sends a closed subset of Baire space (given by its overt representation) to the Sierpiński-space value 1 if the set is empty and ⊥ otherwise.

It is known that for every non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish space X,
  LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W (isEmpty : A(N^N) → S).

Problem. Determine, for each non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish space X, the precise Weihrauch degree of VC_X. More precisely, give a classification (e.g. in terms of standard Weihrauch degrees or a topological invariant of X) that strictly improves upon the bounds LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W (isEmpty : A(N^N) → S).
artifact.status_search_result: The de Brecht–Pauly–Schröder work on overt choice (Computability, 2020) establishes the bounds LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W isEmpty for non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish X and shows VC_X ≡_W LPO on a minimal such space, but no general classification beyond these bounds is reported. No subsequent work resolving the general case was located, so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Overt choice (de Brecht, Pauly, Schröder)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies overt choice on coPolish spaces; relates discontinuity to failure of the Fréchet–Urysohn property; identifies a minimal non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish space on which overt choice is Weihrauch-equivalent to LPO.
status_evidence.claim: Source paper providing the bounds LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W isEmpty without a sharper general classification.

status_evidence.title: Overt choice - IOS Press (Computability)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the overt choice paper, containing the partial classification results.
status_evidence.claim: No improved general classification has been published in the journal version.
